approval.cost: No fee for 3LO integration approval/listing is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: No review is required before real external users can connect. 'When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it. If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.' Once the Distribution sharing toggle is on, any user can authorize via your Authorization URL. The consequence of skipping approval is a warning: 'Users trying to install an unapproved OAuth 2.0 integration are warned that the app has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian.' Optional approval: submit the integration for review via the Marketplace third-party-integration listing path (select 'My app isn't directly installable'; 'you don't need an informative Atlassian Marketplace listing to submit your integration for approval'); the Marketplace team needs access to a test instance of your software to run through setup and configuration. 3LO apps on the Marketplace appear as informational listings only, and 'Enabling sharing doesn't make your app available on the Atlassian Marketplace'.
approval.wait: Marketplace listing guide: 'It usually takes 5-10 business days for our team to start a review' and 'You should hear from a support member within 5 - 10 business days' (stated for the listing process; no duration specific to third-party-integration approvals is given)

blockers.detail: At app creation you choose account-level grant ('a single grant can cover access to multiple sites') or resource-level grant ('consent is limited to the specific site(s) they select'). Known-issue friction for resource-level: 'The consent screen currently requires the user to select the site where they want to install the app... the user would need to repeat the installation process multiple times.' Whether the choice can be changed after creation is not stated in the docs read.
blockers.howToClear: Decide the grant model before creating the app; prefer account-level for multi-site SaaS unless you need site isolation.
blockers.title: Grant-type choice at creation

blockers.detail: 'Only one grant exists per app for a given Atlassian account'; a new consent overrides the old grant's scopes, and 'users who previously consented to the scopes will need to re-consent to the new scopes' when you change scopes in the console. You may only request scopes pre-added to the app, and 'the permissions held by the user an app is acting for always constrain the app, regardless of the app's scopes'. Some REST resources are marked 'Apps can't access this REST resource' and cannot be used with 3LO at all.
blockers.howToClear: Freeze the scope set before distributing the Authorization URL; check each operation's required scopes and 3LO eligibility in advance.
blockers.title: One grant per app per account, and a double scope ceiling

blockers.detail: Refresh tokens rotate: 'You receive a new refresh token as well and the refresh token you used for the request is disabled.' Failing to store the replacement, or using an expired one, returns 403 Forbidden with invalid_grant. A refresh token also dies if 'the user's Atlassian account password has been changed', after which the user must 'initiate the entire authorization flow from the beginning again'.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the replacement refresh token atomically on every refresh and handle invalid_grant as a re-authorization event.
blockers.title: Rotating-refresh failure modes

flavor.recommended: A single, distributable OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app in the Atlassian Developer console, Confluence API added under Permissions, sharing enabled under Distribution
flavor.why: Atlassian explicitly steers vendors this way: 'Build a single, distributable 3LO app for your integration.' The app yields a Client ID and Secret. Confluence scopes come in two families configured on separate console tabs: classic scopes (read:confluence-content.all, write:confluence-content, search:confluence, and others) and granular per-resource scopes (read:page:confluence, read:space:confluence). Include offline_access in the authorize request to receive a refresh token.

humanMust: Create the app in the Developer console, agree to Atlassian's developer terms, and choose the grant type at creation
Add the Confluence API, configure scopes, and set the Callback URL in the console
Copy the Client ID and Secret from Settings
Turn on the 'Enable sharing' toggle under Distribution before external users can connect
name: Confluence
nuances: Rotating refresh tokens carry a 90-day inactivity expiry: 'A rotating refresh token expires if the user is inactive for this period. Each new rotating refresh token resets the inactivity expiry time' (reuse interval/leeway 10 minutes).

API-routing quirk: calls go via api.atlassian.com/ex/confluence/{cloudid}/..., NOT the site's *.atlassian.net domain; discover cloudids via GET api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources, whose id 'is not unique across containers', so you may need to infer the container type from its scopes.

Code flow only: 'OAuth 2.0 (3LO) currently supports the code grant flow only. It does not support the implicit grant flow', which Atlassian acknowledges blocks standalone mobile and web/JavaScript apps (CORS whitelisting is supported for api.atlassian.com).
Admin revocation gap: 'An admin can't revoke a user's access to an app through the Connected Apps user screen. An admin can only choose to uninstall the app to restrict a user's access.'
For the Marketplace path, the App Key 'can't be altered once you set it'.
prerequisites: An Atlassian account for the Developer console
The grant-type decision (account-level vs resource-level) made before creation
A Callback URL (the runtime redirect_uri must match it)

steps.detail: Create > OAuth 2.0 integration: enter a name, agree to Atlassian's developer terms, and choose the grant type (account-level vs resource-level). The app is private by default.
steps.title: Create the app (choose the grant type)

steps.detail: Permissions > Add next to Confluence API > Configure > select scopes on the Classic scopes and Granular scopes tabs; Save. Authorization > Add/Configure next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO) > enter the Callback URL; Save changes. Copy the Client ID and Secret from Settings.
steps.title: Add the Confluence API and scopes; set the callback

steps.detail: Send the user to auth.atlassian.com/authorize with audience=api.atlassian.com, client_id, scope (only scopes already added to the app in the console; include offline_access for a refresh token), redirect_uri, state, response_type=code, prompt=consent. The user consents (and selects the site, for resource-level grants).
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri. Then GET api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources for each site's cloudid, and call the API via api.atlassian.com/ex/confluence/{cloudid}/... with Authorization: Bearer.
steps.title: Exchange the code; discover sites; call the API

steps.detail: POST the token URL with grant_type=refresh_token, client_id, client_secret, refresh_token. Refresh tokens rotate (the used one is disabled) and expire after 90 days of inactivity.
steps.title: Refresh (rotating, 90-day inactivity expiry)

steps.detail: Distribution > turn on 'Enable sharing', then copy the Authorization URL(s) from Authorization > Configure and send the link to your users. Users of an unapproved integration are warned it 'has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian'. Optionally, submit the integration for approval via the Marketplace third-party-integration listing path.
steps.time: ~2 min; optional approval review start 5-10 business days (stated for listings)
steps.title: Enable sharing and distribute

tagline: Atlassian's shared 3LO program, same as Jira: no review before external users can connect once you enable sharing, though unapproved integrations carry a 'not yet reviewed by Atlassian' warning. The real decisions are the grant type chosen at creation and a scope set that, once live, forces re-consent when changed.

time.active: ~15 min of console setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day to distribute; optional Marketplace approval starts review in 5-10 business days (stated for listings)
